title: Military Service Hold Review Proof: Counting Point by Nearness of the Review
content:
**Decision table — Hardship and Protective Holds.** For the current proof of active military duty asked for before a status review of a running Military Service Hold, the point the status review proof due date is counted from depends on how soon the review falls due, in calendar days after the day of the request. Reviews of this tier fall due every 90 calendar days counted from the hold's start date; a review falling due on the day of the request counts as already fallen due, so the review the proof is for is the following one.

| The review falls due | The status review proof is due |
|---|---|
| Within the short-notice days of the request — 7 calendar days or fewer after it | The tier's documentation days, 30 calendar days, after the request |
| Later than 7 days but no later than the tier's review overdue days, 30 calendar days, after the request | 30 documentation days plus the tier's 3 decision days — the decision days counted here as calendar days — that is 33 calendar days after the review's due date |
| Otherwise — more than 30 days after the request | On the last day of the review's overdue window, 30 calendar days after the review's due date |

The days allowed for the status review proof are the calendar days from the request to that due date, a whole number.

## Rows on both sides of each threshold

| Days from the request to the review | Days allowed |
|---|---|
| 1 | 30 |
| 7 | 30 |
| 8 | 41 |
| 30 | 63 |
| 31 | 61 |
| 60 | 90 |

**Example (hypothetical).** Reviews fall due on 1 April, 30 June and 28 September. A request on 10 June finds the review 20 days away — later than 7, no later than 30 — so the proof is due 33 days after 30 June, on 2 August: 53 days allowed.
